Researchers have started looking closely at AI companions, and the early results are worth taking seriously. A 2026 study in Nature Human Behaviour of more than 1,100 Character.AI users found that using a chatbot mainly for companionship was linked with lower well-being, especially for heavy users (Zhang et al., 2026). An OpenAI and MIT Media Lab study found something similar. Emotional use was rare overall, but heavier use went along with worse outcomes for some people (MIT Media Lab, 2025). Neither study proves cause and effect, though the direction was clear enough for us.
